title: Restoration News: 'Anti-American' Spotsylvania school board member running for Dist. 66 seat
text:
Candidates for the 2025 House Nicole Cole (pictured left) and incumbent Bobby Orrock | Nicole Cole for House of Delegates | Delegate Bobby Orrock (Facebook)
Candidates for the 2025 House Nicole Cole (pictured left) and incumbent Bobby Orrock | Nicole Cole for House of Delegates | Delegate Bobby Orrock (Facebook)
Restoration News has reported that the slate of Virginia Democrats' candidates for the 2025 House elections includes individuals with radical ideologies. District 66 candidate Nicole Cole, a current Spotsylvania school board member, is described as being anti-police, pro-Palestine and involved in multiple lawsuits stemming from her role on the board.
According to Restoration News, Cole has declined to recite the Pledge of Allegiance at school board meetings and frequently wears a Palestinian keffiyeh. The outlet also reports that Cole has criticized local law enforcement on social media for engaging in "terror."
Additionally, Cole is involved in ongoing litigation stemming from a 2024 dismissed a misdemeanor assault and battery charge against her for allegedly hitting fellow school board member Lisa Phelps with a door. Judge Gene Woolard ruled there was no proof of criminal intent but noted hostility between members and compared the matter to a domestic dispute, urging the board to focus on educating children, the Fredericksburg Free Press reported.
In response, Cole filed a lawsuit against Phelps alleging malicious prosecution and defamation. Cole is seeking $1 million in damages.
Meanwhile, Cole and fellow Spotsylvania school board members are accused in another lawsuit by the district's former superintendent Mark Taylor over his alleged wrongful termination in March 2024—a move voted on by the board, according to Taylor—for organizing a conservative Christian book fair at Riverbend High School. At time of press, the outcome of an Aug. 27 settlement conference is unknown.
Cole is running against Bobby Orrock, a Republican who has served in the Virginia House of Delegates since 1990. After redistricting in 2024, Orrock shifted from District 54 to District 66. His platform emphasizes lowering taxes, controlling government spending, improving transportation infrastructure, enhancing education, and protecting traditional Virginia values. He highlights his extensive legislative experience and commitment to bipartisan cooperation to advance his policy priorities, according to Ballotpedia.
